.comment: Full example: every setting, plus three common setups (see profiles).
Any key that starts with .comment is a note for you: envtally ignores it, and you can delete or add them anywhere.
Replace the example names and URLs, then run: envtally config validate
Global settings. Every one is optional; the values here are the built-in defaults
(except profile, which has none). Command-line flags override them.
defaults..comment-output: table, tree, compact, markdown, csv or json. Flag: --format
defaults..comment-profile: The app type for apps that do not set "profile" themselves. See profiles below.
defaults..comment-concurrency: How many requests run at the same time.
defaults..comment-timeout: How long to wait for one response: 500ms, 5s, 1m.
defaults..comment-retries: Extra tries when no response arrives at all (refused, timeout). An HTTP answer, even a 500, is never retried.
defaults..comment-insecure: true = accept self-signed or otherwise invalid TLS certificates.
defaults..comment-slowThreshold: An instance slower than this is marked (slow). It does not fail the check.

.comment-envOrder: The order envs are shown in. Envs not listed come after, alphabetically.

.comment: Your own fixed values. Write ${name} to use one in a link template or a header value.
Do not put secrets here; use ${env:NAME} in a header instead (see the internal-api profile).
Links printed by: envtally urls   (envtally never calls them). Name them as you like.
Available: ${project} ${app} ${env} ${host} ${base_url} and anything in vars.
A project or an app can have its own "templates" to override these.
A profile describes one type of app: which paths to call and how to read its version.
springboot, rails and flask are built in and need no entry here.
The three below show the common cases. An app picks one with "profile": "<name>".

springboot..comment: Setup 1: a JSON version endpoint. This is the built-in springboot profile written out, as a reference for your own.
springboot..comment-healthPath: Added to each instance URL. The instance is up when this answers HTTP 2xx.
springboot..comment-healthyWhen: Optional extra rule: the health JSON must also have this field with this value.
springboot..comment-infoPath: Optional second endpoint, called when health passed. The group key is read from its JSON.
.comment-groupKey: What to compare between instances. Each ${a.b} is a field of the info JSON,
Instances of one app/env with the same key are IN SYNC; different keys are DRIFT.

.comment: Setup 2: status only, for apps with no version endpoint (Jenkins, Grafana, a static site, ...).
There is no groupKey, so nothing is compared: the app is UP when the path answers HTTP 2xx.
The response body can be anything (HTML is fine). Add an infoPath to require a second path to answer 2xx too.
jenkins.description: Jenkins: up when the login page loads

internal-api..comment: Setup 3: your own app type, behind authentication.
internal-api.description: Services with /healthz and /meta that need a token

.comment: HTTP request headers, sent with every health and info request for apps using this profile.
Left side: the header name. Right side: its value.
${env:NAME} is replaced by the environment variable NAME when envtally runs,
so the secret is never stored in this file. Set it in your shell first:
PowerShell:  $env:INTERNAL_API_TOKEN = "abc123"
bash / zsh:  export INTERNAL_API_TOKEN=abc123
With that, the line below sends   Authorization: Bearer abc123
If the variable is not set, envtally check stops and names it.
${team} is a plain value from vars above.
Other common forms:
API key:     "X-Api-Key": "${env:MY_API_KEY}"
Basic auth:  "Authorization": "Basic ${env:MY_BASIC_AUTH}"   (the variable holds base64 of user:password)
Fixed value: "X-Client": "envtally"
To see what is sent: envtally check -vv   (header values are shown as [REDACTED]).

projects..comment: The layout is: project -> apps -> envs -> instance URLs. All names are yours to choose.

templates..comment: Overrides the top-level jenkins link for every app in this project.

.comment: No "profile" here, so defaults.profile (springboot) is used.
Each env takes one URL, or a list when the env runs several instances.

ledger..comment: Uses the token-protected profile. A URL may include a path, e.g. behind a gateway.

jenkins..comment: Status only: reported as UP or DOWN, never IN SYNC or DRIFT.
